title: Uptown versus downtown playing styles in New Orleans
summary: Asked about uptown and downtown styles, Lewis says there was no real difference; musicians from both sides played together, and names uptown players and Zeb.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Some of the things you read in some of the books about jazz is that there's a difference between uptown and downtown style, like there was an uptown style and a downtown style, was the difference in the two ways of playing? Do you know anything about that?

No, I don't think so, because we had musicians from downtown who played with uptown musicians uptown and vice versa. I just think it was, one part was called a Creole part of town, like on this side, northern side of Canal Street, and the south side of Canal Street, I played with fellas from uptown like Bud Russel, he was an uptowner, music didn't sound a bit different, and many others, Papa John, Papa John George was a nephew, William George, and so many other people I played with, but, uh, about the night there was a young man who was at the hall, a current man, and he mentioned about his uncle, I forgot his uncle. His uncle was one of the Sam Morgan bass players at one time. His name was, uh, we used to call him T-Boys. His name was, uh, Gilmore. Gilmore. Gilmore. Gilmore. Yeah, yeah. Uh, the last time I saw him was, I had a part of the 30s, uh, in Bunky when I was a Billy GD. So they didn't make much difference because, uh, the Creole people, uh, they said it was different, but there's no difference. I don't know, it's a bit different because, uh, there were a really good, a lot of good musicians uptown, uh, there seemed like there were more musicians uptown than downtown. You think, for instance, like, uh, Redhead's, uh, band, already had a very good kind of player with his name, he's Zeb.

Zeb played with him before. I had played with him. Zeb. Zeb. Uh, he had, uh, uh, uh, Maurice French, uh, uh, Papa French was a fan of him. The band was, uh, uh, singing a band. He was only. He also had the other uncle that played Bees only. Then in advance, uh, was sitting around putting a string Bees down. Everybody was hidden. Bees behind. Bees on. Like Chester. Jim Lillard. Jim Lillard. And many other. Jax. I knew he was good. He was good. I knew he did something.
